A flat 128 KB WRAM image ($7E at offset 0, $7F at 0x10000) -- the file `ct.exe --peek` writes alongside its framebuffer as `<out>.wram`. CATALOGUED 2026-08-30 to close the one-command gate: before this, 37 of the 62 declared fixtures had no sha256 at all, so tools/preflight.py hard-failed on 'EXTRA' and exited WITHOUT RUNNING A SINGLE CHECK. ⚠ ITS PROVENANCE WAS NOT RECORDED WHEN THE CHECK WAS ADDED and is NOT reconstructed here -- writing a plausible-looking recipe would be worse than admitting the gap, because the next reader would trust it. What the sha256 above DOES guarantee is the thing the gate exists for: this is the exact byte sequence the consuming check(s) were pinned against, so a silent substitution or a regeneration with different contents now shows up as MISMATCH instead of as a quietly different green. If this file is lost, the check must be RE-DERIVED from the ROM/oracle, not re-guessed. Consumed by: field-battle-ambush-generic-dissolve, field-battle-enemy-name-list.

The oracle's own WRAM with the Form screen (option 4) OPEN, so the check grades the RENDER and not the menu-open stat pass. Regenerate: build/ct.exe --peek saves/battle_re/party3_field.state out.raw --btnscript "0:4,200:3,0:40,80:2,0:6,80:2,0:6,80:2,0:6,80:2,0:6,100:2,0:40" (X, Right x4, A) and take out.raw.wram. WHY THE POST-OPEN CAPTURE AND NOT THE FIELD ONE: the ROM RECOMPUTES each character's derived attack/defence at menu open -- C2/9137 MVNs 11 bytes from $7E:9B1C into sheet+0x36 (writer C2:9160), built by C2/916E out of the equipment via C2/9261 with the caps at FF/CF33 and a per-charId pass through the C2/91DB jump table -- and a raw FIELD capture carries stale values (party3_field has Frog's +0x3D reading 229 where the menu computes 18). That stat engine is the same C1/CF15 + FD/B033 subsystem battle.c already names as a boundary, so this fixture keeps the boundary OUT of the pixel check instead of pinning a frame that shows its symptom.
